source.title: Investigating Sensitive Directions in GPT-2: An Improved Baseline and Comparative Analysis of SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how SAE feature-direction perturbations affect GPT-2-small outputs, but does not measure feature splitting, relations between small- and large-dictionary features, nested families, absorption, or whether splitting is an SAE-objective artifact.
record.gate_note: The paper reports sensitive-direction results for SAE feature directions, including comparisons by SAE type and L0. These findings concern output sensitivity, not splitting or the feature relationships named in the claim versions. Its cited work is not treated as evidence for this study.
record.test_reason: The study runs sensitive-direction perturbation experiments on GPT2-small SAE feature and error directions, measuring KL divergence. It does not compare features across dictionary sizes or examine splitting, feature families, absorption, decomposition into smaller-SAE latents, or objective-driven splitting. It cites Towards Monosemanticity only as background on SAEs. 'cites_only' fits, though no splitting result is cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude three things. SAE reconstruction errors are no longer pathologically large against realistic (cov-random/real mixture) baselines. GPT2-small is more sensitive to lower-L0 SAE features. End-to-end SAE features do not have stronger output effects than traditional SAE features.
record.recipe_differences: The study conducts sensitive-direction perturbation experiments; it does not test a feature-splitting method or measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-direction effects vary with SAE type and L0. The paper also reports different L0 effects for SAE reconstruction-error directions at small versus large perturbation lengths.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT2-small layer 6, SAE decoder directions change outputs more than isotropic random directions. Lower-L0 SAE feature directions cause larger KL changes, for local, e2e and e2e+ds SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature-direction output impact exceeds isotropic random directions and increases as SAE L0 decreases.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale at NeurIPS 2024
record.problems: The authors note that they rely primarily on mean KL, which may oversimplify the perturbation curves. The reported feature-direction findings do not measure splitting or feature-family geometry.

untested.parts: All: no comparison of features across dictionary sizes.
All: no splitting analysis in any model or SAE release.
All: no feature-family geometry or hierarchy analysis.
All: no parent/child firing or absorption measure.
All: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents.
All: L0 and SAE-type comparisons concern output sensitivity, not splitting.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are accurate to Section 4.2 and Figure 4, and correctly carry versions ['none']. Rows r4-r6 compare across L0, not dictionary size, and do not bear on splitting.

versions.untested_parts: Whether larger dictionaries replace a coarse feature with finer features that cover its inputs and lie near its direction.
Whether the splitting pattern holds at scale or across open SAE releases.
Whether split features form nested, geometrically close families mirroring a conceptual hierarchy.
Whether parent features fail to fire where child features take over, or whether size and sparsity changes remedy that pattern.
Whether larger latents decompose into smaller-latent combinations, and whether larger SAEs add novel latents.
Whether splitting is produced by the SAE objective on correlated or hierarchical inputs, or whether Matryoshka SAEs change or reduce splitting.

relation.reason: It cites Bricken et al. (the original source) for SAEs and the linear representation hypothesis, but never discusses, uses or tests feature splitting.

tranche.reason: This is a sensitive-direction perturbation study measuring KL divergence. It compares SAEs by L0 and type, not by dictionary size, and does not look at splitting, feature families, absorption or decomposition.

source_check.notes: All six rows match Section 4.2 and Figure 4 at layer 6 resid_pre, with features chosen as alive but not active. The text gives no numbers for them (figure only). The L0 comparison varies sparsity, not dictionary size, and measures output sensitivity, not splitting, so it bears on no feature-splitting version.
